messages:
Riley: Hey folks - had to go to an ER while traveling in Lisbon last week. Paid the hospital up front in euros. Carrier sent an EOB but it looks like they applied a different exchange rate and I'm being balance-billed for ~€250. I have the hospital receipt, the payment card statement showing the exact USD charge, and the carrier EOB. How do I get reimbursed for the extra amount and contest the exchange rate?

Nina (People Ops): Ugh, sorry you had to deal with that overseas. Two parallel actions: 1) File a claim reimbursement to carrier with the itemized hospital bill + proof of payment (card statement or bank receipt). Ask the carrier to apply the transaction date FX conversion or provide their FX methodology. 2) Submit a manual reimbursement request to Redwood benefits with all docs and we can file an appeal/coordination letter on your behalf to the carrier if the carrier's FX calc looks wrong.

Riley: Do you need an official translation of the receipt? It's in Portuguese but has numeric totals.

Ben: (was on the trip) Short answer: usually not for claims where amounts are clear. The carrier often accepts numeric receipts without translation, but include a short note translating key fields (total charged, paid, patient responsibility). If the receipt language is ambiguous, a quick one-paragraph translation PDF helps speed things up.

Nina (People Ops): For Redwood's internal request, upload: itemized bill, proof of payment (card statement), carrier EOB, and a one-paragraph translation if not in English. Use subject "International ER claim - [Your Name] - [DOS]" and mark "EXPEDITE" if the hospital is threatening collections. We'll also include a letter stating this was emergency care while traveling which sometimes triggers emergency/Urgent care rules with the carrier.

Riley: How long does an appeal take? The hospital sent a dunning notice so this is a bit time-sensitive.

Nina (People Ops): Appeals can take 14-30 business days at the carrier level. When you route through us with the EXPEDITE flag and proof of payment, we usually get provisional hold requests or payment extensions from the provider while the appeal is pending. If you want, we can draft a one-page provider hold letter you can send to the hospital billing office.

BenefitsBot: Upload portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/upload (choose "International/Emergency"). Provider letter template: https://benefits.redwood.com/templates/provider-hold-letter.pdf

Riley: Please send the provider hold letter. I'll upload the docs now and include the card charge screenshot. Thanks for the help. :pray:
